item.text:
It’s understandable to want an explanation, particularly given your qualifications and how far you progressed. **An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence that your sex counted against you.** It is a fact about the process, but not enough to infer bias—just as an all-men panel would not, by itself, establish discrimination against a woman.

Your completed PhD, publication record and teaching experience give you reasonable grounds to ask how the decision was reached. But the announcement isn’t a full comparison: industry experience, teaching performance, research quality, subject specialism and interview answers may have carried weight. More papers don’t automatically mean a stronger application under the advertised criteria.

I would focus first on **whether the university followed its stated criteria and procedures**, rather than the panel members’ sex:

- Check whether a completed PhD was required at application, by the start date, or merely preferred.
- Follow up on your request, asking for the assessment criteria, their weighting, feedback on your application and whatever selection records they can disclose.
- Check the recruitment policy for panel-composition requirements and the complaint or appeal deadlines. Don’t assume that waiting for a response pauses those deadlines.

You could write:

> I am following up on my request of [date] for written feedback. Please confirm when I can expect a response, including how my application was assessed against the advertised criteria. Please also let me know the procedure and deadline for requesting a review of the selection process.

Sex-based comments, inconsistent treatment of candidates, departures from essential requirements, or an explicit preference could make a discrimination concern more substantial. A breach of a panel-composition rule would also be worth raising, though it would not automatically prove discriminatory selection.

**For now, pursue transparency rather than lead with an allegation about the panel.** What country was the university in? That determines your rights to reasons, records and review, and any relevant deadlines.
